hardening: The kill switch is read once, at startup: `revoked = grant_file.revoked || kill_file.exists()` (payer.rs:185-191), and every invoice is decided before any payment moves (244-270), so `touch`ing the kill file mid-run stops nothing — including invoices already decided and not yet broadcast. docs/BOUNDED-PAYER.md:33-34 says the switch stops 'the next decision', which overstates it for a run in flight; its own limits section ('no revocation of in-flight payments') partly covers this. Design limit with no privileged actor; the smallest improvement is re-checking the kill file before each broadcast.

The expiry verdict rests on a caller-supplied clock that is never recorded: `--now` overrides the clock (payer.rs:162, 169-172), PayerDecision carries no decision time or clock (observation:200-214), and paid reasons embed no timestamp — so a run's expiry verdict cannot be reproduced from its artifacts, and a runner distinct from the grant author can un-expire an immutable grant with no trace. In this repo the grant author and the runner are the same principal, so this is not a privilege gain (validation rule 3), but it is why candidate zanary/payer-expiry-text-compare cannot be caught after the fact; recording `decided_at` (and gating `--now` as test-only) fixes both.

The payer-policy boundary is weaker than its module doc: it claims to catch a payment 'after the grant expired' (payer_policy.rs:6-8) but has no time input at all; it never cross-checks the ledger against run.payments (a paid decision with zero backing payments passes, H6); and its internal-error rule keys on the literal reason prefix "error:" (payer_policy.rs:68) that the reference payer never writes (it aborts instead, payer.rs:298-309), so 'should have paid but errored' is structurally undetectable for this payer. Fix: carry decided_at plus the paid txid in PayerDecision and re-derive/verify both in check().

The grant file format fails open on unrecognised or misspelled keys: no `deny_unknown_fields`, and every absent security field defaults to a wider value — budget 50,000,000 zat, cap 10,000,000 zat, empty allowlist (any receiver is allowed, payer.rs:222-227 documents it), missing expiry -> now + 30 days (payer.rs:49-70, 173-184). The widened grant is what gets recorded, so payer-policy validates against the widening (offline check H4). Same principal supplies the file, so hardening rather than a privilege gain; the fix is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on Grant plus making budget/cap/allowlist/expires_at required fields.

hardening: Identity signer accepted: a receipt whose `signer` is the 32-byte all-zero encoding (the Pallas identity point) verifies for any payload (executed: signature r=B, s=1 -> `signature : VALID`, exit 0), because reddsa 0.5.2 deliberately admits the identity as an Orchard verification key and pasta_curves decodes all-zero bytes as the identity. A real Orchard `ak` can never be the identity, so a self-contained receipt format should reject it explicitly (a `signer` of all zeros is otherwise a key whose 'private' scalar 0 is public).

Verifier more permissive than the schema it says it implements: uppercase hex passes validate_claim for `txid`/`memo_sha256` (receipt.rs:301 uses is_ascii_hexdigit, and the receipt.rs:303 error text claims lowercase) and for `signer`/`signature`/`attestation.*`, while schemas/zanary-receipt-v1.json requires ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ / ^[0-9a-f]{128}$; the attestation's own field shapes are only checked on the --fvk path. Two shipped validators therefore disagree about the same artifact (executed: uppercase-txid receipt exits 0 with `claim ok`).
